subject: Proposal: split-model for compliance addons (audit logs / KMS / residency) and slate credit
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@greengate.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: split-model for compliance addons (audit logs / KMS / residency) and slate credit

Hi Nora,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — appreciated the clarity on Greengate's rollout priorities (pilot -> phased clinical scale across three regions). Per our conversation I attached a compact price grid and an initial implementation SOW draft for the compliance add-ons you asked about: audit-log retention tiers, KMS vs HSM seat options, and a regional residency surcharge.

A few pragmatic options we think will map to your procurement ask:
- Option A (Pilot-friendly): 90-day audit log retention, shared-managed KMS (no HSM), one-time onboarding fee, 6-month slate credit (applied as monthly credits) to offset pilot implementation.
- Option B (Scale-ready): 365-day retention, dedicated KMS + 1 HSM seat, residency enabled for US-East + EU (as scope), implementation amortized across a 12-month credit schedule tied to committed spend.
- Option C (Sovereign-heavy): 365-day retention, multi-HSM seats, on-prem residency deployment (higher capex). Pricing is listed in the attached grid.

Two asks from our side to make the economics clean for procurement:
1) A committed monthly minimum for the 12-month credit amortization in Option B (we used $75k/mo in the spreadsheet as an example).
2) Agreement on evidence delivery cadence (SOC2 snapshot + one compliance workshop during onboarding).

If you want, we can lay the three options into a simple concession ladder: larger committed spend -> higher onboarding credit + reduced residency surcharge. Laura and Ben are looped to translate to contract language once we pick a direction.

Next step: would you be able to confirm whether Greengate prefers amortized credits (Option B) vs a one-time implementation credit (Option A)? I can follow up with a redline-friendly summary for procurement.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment(s): GG_Redwood_compliance_price_grid_20270506.xlsx, SOW-draft-compliance-activation.docx
From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@greengate.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greengate.health>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: split-model for compliance addons (audit logs / KMS / residency) and slate credit

Jordan —

Thanks for the proposal and for the clear options. A couple of clarifications from procurement and engineering here:

- Residency: Greengate needs US commercial-only for pilot, but EU residency will be required for Q3 (so Option B's ability to enable EU later is important).
- KMS vs HSM: our security team would prefer a dedicated HSM for any PHI-handling workloads; however procurement is sensitive to seat-based recurring charges.
- Credits: procurement prefers a one-time implementation credit applied to the first two invoices instead of a 12-month amortization — that simplifies our forecasting.

Can you share how a one-time credit would change the numbers in Option B? Specifically: if we keep the $75k/mo commit but convert the 12-month amortized onboarding credit to a one-time credit equal to 6 months of the onboarding value, what would the net TCO look like for year one vs year two?

Also attaching SOC2 snapshot you requested (redacted). We will need a formal evidence delivery timeline in the contract.

On the HSM seat question — can we get a proposal that offers a blended HSM charge (first seat at list, additional seats at a discount) and a reduced residency surcharge if the commit hits $150k/mo? Procurement likes clear trigger thresholds.

Thanks,
Nora Chen
Head of Product Operations, Greengate Health
[nora.chen@greengate.health]

Attachment(s): SOC2_snapshot_Mar2027.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@greengate.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>; Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>; Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: split-model for compliance addons (audit logs / KMS / residency) and slate credit

Nora — thanks for the quick read and the SOC2 snapshot. I pulled finance and product into a short concession plan below so procurement has concrete options to evaluate. See the attached revised price grid (high level summary here):

Concession sketch (if Greengate signs the $75k/mo commit):
- One-time implementation credit: equal to 6 months of the implementation line in Option B (applied to invoices 1 and 2). This replaces amortized credits.
- HSM seat pricing: first seat at $18,000/year, additional seats at 40% off (so $10,800/year). If you hit $150k/mo commit, first seat drops to $12,000/year and add-on seats are 55% off.
- Residency surcharge: baseline surcharge 12% of hosted usage for EU enablement; with $150k/mo commit the surcharge steps down to 6%.
- Audit log retention tiers: pilot 90-day at no surcharge, 365-day adds $X per 100k users (see grid).
- Evidence cadence: SOC2 snapshot (provided), onboarding workshop (included), quarterly evidence bundle for 12 months (included).

Quick Year 1 / Year 2 TCO sketch (numbers in attached grid):
- Year 1 (with one-time credit): Year 1 net spend ~ 0.89 * baseline (credit applied) — I put the example numbers against your $75k/mo baseline in GG_Redwood_compliance_price_grid_20270506.xlsx.
- Year 2: baseline plus residency surcharge if EU enabled; without additional credits.

If Greengate prefers an amortized approach instead, finance says we can still do 12-month amortization but the per-month credit would be slightly higher to reach same total concession. The one-time credit option is cleaner for your forecasting, but amortization helps smooth Redwood's revenue recognition which some legal teams prefer.

Next steps:
- If this concession sketch looks acceptable, Laura will draft contract language representing the $75k commit + one-time credit + the HSM blended pricing and residency step-down.
- Can procurement confirm the preferred commit threshold ($75k vs $150k/mo) and whether the EU residency enablement should be gated to a milestone (we suggest 'production go-live in EU region' as the trigger).

I'm happy to hop on a 25-minute call with procurement + engineering to finalize the triggers — Laura, Ben and Rachel are standing by.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): GG_Redwood_compliance_price_grid_20270506.xlsx, SOW-draft-compliance-activation.docx
From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@greengate.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greengate.health>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: split-model for compliance addons (audit logs / KMS / residency) and slate credit

Jordan / team —

This looks good and very actionable. Procurement prefers the $75k/mo commit to start (we can revisit uplift later). We accept the one-time credit equal to 6 months of the implementation line, and the blended HSM seat pricing is acceptable subject to contract language.

Two small asks before we route to legal for a redline:
1) Insert a clause that the residency surcharge step-down to 6% is retroactive to the date of EU enablement invoice (not just future invoices).
2) Add a 30-day SLA response time for evidence requests during the first 6 months (we need faster turnaround on compliance artifacts while onboarding).

If you can get a draft with those two items, procurement will circulate to legal and economics should be able to sign off quickly. Can we aim for a redline-ready contract by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Nora
Head of Product Operations, Greengate Health
